newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson plant downs tools over Daewoo buy.
newsitem.headline: Thomson plant downs tools over Daewoo buy.

text.p: Four trade unions at the Angers factory in the Thomson SA electronics group called on its 1,370 workers to down tools for an hour on Friday at 1000 GMT, to protest against the planned sale of the Multimedia arm to Daewoo Electronics.

"The speech by (Prime Minister Alain)Juppe on Wednesday on (television channel) France 3 that Thomson Multimedia has negative value of 14 billion francs ($2.7 billion) was the trigger for our anger," Odile Coquereau, an official of the communist-led CGT union said. The factory, in western France, makes digital television sets.
"We denounce the cut price sale of Thomson," she said.
The union is studying further action, the union official said.
Thomson Multimedia employees have called on the company's 5,500 workers, employed in 11 sites throughout France, to demonstrate in Paris on November 20 against the sale to South Korea's Daewoo.

The French government wants to sell Thomson to the Lagardere conglomerate for a symbolic one franc, allowing Lagardere to retain the CSF defence arm and dispose of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo, also for one franc.
Multimedia made a first-half loss of three billion francs and has debt of 14 billion francs.
The socialist and communist groups in the lower house National Assembly have called for a committee of inquiry into the conditions of Thomson's privatisation.
